hint: The amplitude is the number multiplying the sine.

hints.text: The amplitude is the number multiplying the sine.
In $y = a\sin(x)$, the amplitude is $a$ — how far the wave swings from the middle.

explanation: A sine graph is a WAVE that rises and falls forever around a middle level.
Amplitude is how far it swings above and below that middle, and it is the number in front of $\sin$.
In $y = 4\sin(x)$ that number is $4$, so the amplitude is $4$.

alternativeExplanations.title: From the highest and lowest points
steps: Plain sin(x) rides between −1 and 1. Multiplying by 4 stretches it to between −4 and 4.

alternativeExplanations.title: The jump-rope picture
steps: Imagine a jump rope shaken up and down. The middle of the rope is the midline.
The amplitude is how far your hand lifts the rope above that middle — here, 4 units.
